title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with finite-dimensional Bergman spaces
summary: We construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. Based on this example, for any integers $n \geq 3, d \geq 1$, we further construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the Bergman space is $d$-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck's conjecture.
